title: O Word of God Incarnate
description: O Word of God Incarnate in Tonic Solfa to EWING, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Walsham How wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 113.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to EWING; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Word of God In-car-nate, O Wis-dom from on high, O Truth un-changed, un-chang-ing, O Light of our dark sky,— We praise Thee for the ra-diance That from the hal-lowed page, A lan-tern to our foot-steps, Shines on from age to age.

lines: O Light of our dark sky,—
We praise Thee for the radiance
Shines on from age to age.
The Church from her dear Master
And still that light she lifteth
O’er all the earth to shine.
Where gems of truth are stored;
It is the chart and compass
Mid mists and rocks and quicksands,
Still guides, O Christ, to Thee.
Oh, make Thy Church, dear Savior,
Thy true light as of old;
By this their path to trace,
They see Thee face to face.

licence: Public domain: William Walsham How died in 1897.
credits: Words by William Walsham How (1823–1897), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to EWING by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
